note: Data platforms. Use one as a primary provider to design a data-centred system, or add one next to your compute provider with --also (for example --cloud aws --also neon).

any: Runs Python data and AI web apps next to your lakehouse data.

any.caveat: Databricks Apps suit data and AI applications, not general-purpose web back ends.

any: Databricks Data Intelligence Platform (lakehouse with Databricks SQL)
A lakehouse for analytics, SQL warehousing and machine learning over open table formats.
A managed vector index kept in sync with lakehouse tables.
Serves your own and foundation models behind an API.
Governed file storage in your lakehouse.
A managed PostgreSQL for application data next to the lakehouse.

any.caveat: Lakebase is newer than the rest of the platform; check its availability and regions.

any: Databricks system tables and audit logs
Usage, lineage and audit data as queryable tables.
Databricks identity and access management (Unity Catalog)
Controls who can reach data and models inside the platform.

any.caveat: This governs platform users, not your application's end users.

gaps.edge: Put your own CDN and firewall in front of any public app.
gaps.network: Use your cloud's private networking for the Databricks workspace.
gaps.cache: Use a managed Redis from your cloud.
gaps.secrets: Use Databricks secret scopes or your cloud's secrets manager.

server: Builds and runs full-stack web apps on Google Cloud, with a CDN in front.
serverless: Runs your server-side code per event or request and scales automatically.

serverless.caveat: Each invocation has a time limit, and streaming routes need testing.

any: Serves your front end from Google's CDN.
Routes requests to your functions and App Hosting back end.
Serves cached content close to users.

any.caveat: Add Firebase App Check and Google Cloud Armor if you need request filtering.

any: A serverless document database with real-time sync.

any.caveat: Firestore is not MongoDB-compatible; code written for a MongoDB driver needs a rewrite of its data layer.

any: Firebase Data Connect with Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL
A managed PostgreSQL with a generated, typed API for your apps.
Vector similarity search over Firestore documents.
Managed sign-in with email, social and phone providers.
Object storage for user uploads with security rules.
Secret Manager through Cloud Functions parameters
Stores credentials and hands them to your functions.
Crash reports and performance traces for your apps.
Calls Google's Gemini models from your apps without exposing keys.

gaps.network: Firebase is a managed platform without a network you configure; use Google Cloud VPC for Cloud SQL.
gaps.cache: Use Memorystore on Google Cloud or an external Redis.
gaps.registry: Not needed: Firebase builds from source.

any: A fully managed MongoDB on AWS, Azure or Google Cloud, with backups and private connectivity.
Vector similarity search inside the same Atlas cluster.
Full-text search inside the same Atlas cluster.
Metrics, slow-query analysis and alerts for the cluster.
Private connectivity from your cloud network to the cluster.

any.caveat: Set up the matching private link on your compute provider.

gaps.compute: Atlas hosts data only; run the application on another provider.
gaps.db_postgres: Atlas is a MongoDB service; use a PostgreSQL service for relational data.
gaps.cache: Use a managed Redis from your compute provider.
gaps.storage: Use object storage from your compute provider.

any: A serverless PostgreSQL that scales to zero, with branching for previews and tests.

any.caveat: Connect through the pooled connection string from serverless functions to avoid exhausting connections.

any: Vector similarity search inside the same Neon PostgreSQL.

gaps.compute: Neon hosts a database only; run the application on another provider.
gaps.cache: Use a managed Redis from your compute provider.
gaps.storage: Use object storage from your compute provider.

any: A managed cloud data warehouse for analytics, with separate storage and compute.
Hybrid vector and keyword search over Snowflake data.
Hosted language models and AI functions that run next to your data.
Runs containers next to your Snowflake data.

any.caveat: Best for data and AI services, not general-purpose web back ends.

any: File storage inside Snowflake for loading and unloading data.
Snowflake ACCOUNT_USAGE views and event tables
Usage, query history and logs as queryable views.

gaps.db_postgres: Snowflake Postgres is not part of this catalogue; use a managed PostgreSQL for transactional data.
gaps.cache: Use a managed Redis from your compute provider.
gaps.network: Use private connectivity from your cloud to Snowflake.

any: Runs server-side TypeScript close to users, scaling automatically.

any.caveat: Edge Functions run Deno-based TypeScript, so existing back ends may need changes.

any: A managed PostgreSQL with backups, Row Level Security and an instant API.
Vector similarity search inside the same Postgres.
Managed sign-in with email, social and enterprise providers.
Object storage for files and uploads with access policies.
Routes requests to the database API, auth and functions.
Encrypted secrets for the database and functions.
Logs and usage reports for the database, auth and functions.

gaps.edge: Put Cloudflare or a similar CDN and firewall in front of public endpoints.
gaps.cache: Use a managed Redis from your compute provider.
gaps.network: Restrict database access with network restrictions and SSL enforcement.
gaps.db_mongo: Supabase is PostgreSQL; use MongoDB Atlas for a MongoDB driver.
gaps.queue_kafka: Use Supabase Queues for simple jobs, or Confluent Cloud for Kafka.
